analysisWe need to infer the rule mapping each input sentence to output. Let's examine examples.

1. "I think that this is interesting." => "It is my opinion that this is interesting."
Transformation: Replace "I think that" with "It is my opinion that". Also change perspective? "I think that" -> "It is my opinion that". So rephrase first-person opinion to impersonal.

2. "Please call once you get there." => "Please call upon your arrival."
Transformation: "once you get there" -> "upon your arrival". So replace phrase with more formal equivalent.

3. "The lawyer I met yesterday was helpful. " => "The lawyer whom I met yesterday was helpful."
Add "whom" after lawyer, making relative clause explicit.

4. "I considered many approaches." => "Various approaches were considered."
Active voice first-person to passive, and "many" -> "Various". So convert to passive voice and replace "many" with "Various".

5. "I can't stand his temper." => "I cannot tolerate his temper."
Contraction expanded, "can't stand" -> "cannot tolerate". So replace idiom with formal synonym.

6. "She looks like her sister." => "She resembles her sister."
Replace "looks like" with "resembles".

7. "Can you do all these tasks?" => "Would you be able to accomplish all these tasks?"

Slang "fire" -> "incredibly good". So replace slang with formal phrase.
